lifecycle.note: Google announced Jules will become read-only after November 11, 2026 and wind down December 31, 2026. The notice offers an export of configuration and session history; code, branches and PRs remain on GitHub.

lifecycle.continuation: The notice points to Google Antigravity as a product informed by Jules learnings; it does not promise automatic migration or continued Jules execution. GitHub code and PRs remain with their repositories.

sources.title: Getting started
sources.locator: Login; Connect GitHub; first task; notifications
sources.finding: Jules uses Google identity, authorized GitHub repositories, a cloud VM and AGENTS.md. Shutdown dates supersede the generic onboarding guide.

sources.title: Running tasks
sources.locator: Visual context; feedback; pause; issue label
sources.finding: Tasks accept initial images, in-run feedback and pause controls. A jules issue label starts work through the GitHub integration.

sources.title: Reviewing plans & giving feedback
sources.finding: Jules presents a step plan that can be revised, but the guide says it eventually auto-approves after navigation away.

sources.title: Environment setup
sources.finding: Every task uses an Ubuntu VM with developer tools; successful setup scripts can be snapshotted for later tasks.

sources.title: Reviewing code changes
sources.locator: Activity feed; diffs; pushing to GitHub
sources.finding: Jules shows changed-file diffs, accepts feedback and can publish a branch or PR after the user action.

sources.title: Limits and plans
sources.finding: The published tiers list daily and concurrent task quotas; wind-down dates limit future evaluation access.

sources.title: FAQ
sources.locator: Leaving while working; training; setup scripts
sources.finding: Cloud tasks continue after leaving the app; private repository content is excluded from model training according to the FAQ.

sources.title: Scheduled tasks
sources.finding: Jules has cloud recurring tasks configured with frequency and cadence; edit behavior has later changelog updates and is not inferred from this older guide.

sources.title: Jules REST API quickstart
sources.finding: The alpha REST API exposes sources, sessions and activities using API keys; stability is explicitly experimental.

sources.title: Jules Tools reference
sources.finding: Jules Tools logs into Google, lists/creates remote sessions and pulls results; it does not run the coding worker locally.

sources.title: Jules Turndown
sources.finding: Google announces read-only after November 11 and wind-down December 31, 2026; configuration and full session history can be exported locally.

sources.title: Jules FAQ
sources.locator: Leave while working; Failure handling; Training; Free access
sources.finding: Jules can work after the user leaves the app, notifies plan/task completion, retries failed steps and never trains on private repository content. A recurring no-cost plan is documented. Setup scripts do not support long-lived servers.

sources.title: Jules Limits and Plans
sources.finding: Free, Pro and Ultra document daily limits of 15/100/300 and concurrent limits of 3/15/60. Paid Google AI plans require individual Gmail accounts; business/Workspace upgrade routes are not yet available.

sources.title: Jules Environment setup
sources.finding: Repository setup scripts install dependencies and run discrete checks. Successful Run and Snapshot captures the environment for future tasks, including preinstalled runtimes and tools.

sources.title: Reviewing Jules code
sources.finding: Jules exposes activity/errors, per-file and expanded diffs, real-time feedback, downloadable changes and a completion summary with runtime, files, lines and branch/commit details. Publish branch/PR controls export changes.

sources.title: Jules REST API
sources.finding: Alpha REST API uses X-Goog-Api-Key, with up to three keys. Sessions and activities expose plans, messages and progress. Alpha specifications and keys may change.

sources.title: Repoless, outputs and activity filters
sources.finding: REST API can start sessions without a repository and return changed-file outputs in Git patch format. Activities are immutable records with timestamp filters and can reconstruct a session.

sources.title: Jules Planning
sources.finding: Jules creates a step plan after setup and revises it from chat feedback. Approve plan starts execution, but the documentation says a timer may auto-approve when the user leaves.

sources.title: Jules Errors and failures
sources.finding: Failed steps are retried where possible, including network/install faults. Persistent failures get a failed state and UI badge. Humans can change setup/prompt and rerun.

sources.title: Jules gains memory
sources.finding: Jules saves preferences, nudges and corrections during a task and references them in later same-repository tasks. Memory can be toggled per repository under Knowledge in repo settings.

sources.title: Jules CI Fixer and authorship
sources.finding: Jules receives failed GitHub Actions checks on its own PRs, fixes and resubmits. User-level settings choose Jules-only, coauthored or user-only commits.

sources.title: Update Scheduled Tasks
sources.finding: The dated release adds schedule editing, pause and resume without deleting and recreating the task; the undated schedule guide still says editing is unavailable.

sources.title: Jules web-app testing
sources.finding: Jules can render and verify a frontend, returning a screenshot with the code changes. The base image includes Playwright.
